fieldValues.title: Composition renders select sections, never re-point them
fieldValues.decision_question: When a render request asks for part of a composition, does it select a section, or substitute a container into every section, as `render composition --container` does today?
fieldValues.context: The exercise 'Render one section of a composition' (c636bb69, checked 2026-11-04 against srs-rust 99e5594, release v0.1.0-build.576) found that the spec composition has nine container-subset sections, one per Part, and that `srs render composition --container <Part>` renders all nine sections against that one container (about 905 kB instead of about 100 kB): on render, --container silently re-points every section. `--instance` scopes to a record and its subtree but cannot name a concept container, so srs#983 splits the rendered markdown by headings in a script (scripts/lib/agent-pages.mjs). srs-rust#1510 (open) plans a --section selector and one meaning for --container but states 'Ruling: none'. RFC-043 puts order on the Container and RFC-036 keeps presentation in the view layer; neither rules on partial selection. srs#851 (RFC-050, Draft, open) would stop compositions naming containers. The analyst recommended 'B for --container (one meaning, never a silent re-point) with A's selector'. Decision 0b1c25b1 requires a recorded ruling before the Third-party-ready group files a CLI, payload or WASM contract change; this record is that ruling. Any later change to section shape stays with RFC-050.
fieldValues.friction: A publisher who wants one Part's page gets nine sections of the wrong content, silently, and has to split the markdown by headings in a client script, which is a client reimplementing a selection the core owns (SP-123, SP-05).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. A section selector, and a container option that only fills what a section leaves open (recommended, the analyst's B with A's selector): render accepts a section by index or title and renders it with its own filter and dispatch; --container never replaces a container a section already names (refused if every section names its own). Leads to: per-Part pages from the core, and a --container meaning that survives RFC-050, where sections name none and the request supplies it. 2. A selector only (option A): --container keeps re-pointing, so the silent wrong render stays possible. 3. Redefine --container alone (option B without a selector): one meaning, but no way to name a section whose source is not a container. 4. Wait for RFC-050 (option C): keeps the heading splitter and the silent re-point for as long as RFC-050 stays Draft.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One meaning per option, and never a silent re-point (SP-06): a request the render cannot honour as asked is refused. The same selection must exist in CLI and WASM (capability layering), so clients do not split output. Evolution: the ruling must still hold if RFC-050 removes container literals from sections; 'the container option fills only what a section leaves open' holds in both shapes. Out of scope: whether each Part should instead be its own Composition.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A request to render part of a composition selects whole sections, and never substitutes a container for one a section already names.
fieldValues.rationale: Today's behaviour gives a plausible but wrong document without warning, which is worse than either a refusal or a missing feature. Selecting by section puts per-Part rendering in the core where RFC-036 places presentation, and limiting the container option to what a section leaves open is the reading that stays true after RFC-050.
fieldValues.revisit_when: RFC-050 leaves Draft with a section shape in which 'a section names a container' no longer applies or selection by section is ambiguous; or a publisher needs a selection finer than a section (a single subtree inside one) that --instance does not cover.
fieldValues.next_steps: After ratification: srs-rust#1510 is reshaped to this ruling and filed as ready group work; srs#983's splitter is retired once it lands. Tracked as linked issues.
